topic: Cross-version multimodal document grounding: stable region and element lineage across revised attachments, message-to-attachment referring expressions, revised-workbook provenance, and end-to-end hierarchical evidence identifiers from version through page, region or cell to answer span.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Broad umbrella for machine learning applied to document images and digitally born documents, including OCR, layout analysis, classification, information extraction, table processing, and question answering.
seed_audit.main_risk: Far broader than the target capabilities; by itself it says nothing about version lineage, exact evidence grounding, attachment references, or workbook semantics.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Document classification, OCR-only systems, invoice extraction, generic form processing, commercial document-processing surveys, and parser benchmarks.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Broad and partly industry-driven label for automated extraction, understanding, classification, and reasoning over documents.
seed_audit.main_risk: Less standardized academically than narrower task names and frequently used for product platforms rather than a precise research task.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Commercial intelligent-document-processing systems, workflow automation, OCR pipelines, and high-level surveys without region-level grounding.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Understanding documents in which text, two-dimensional layout, typography, visual elements, and document structure jointly carry meaning.
seed_audit.main_risk: Strong umbrella terminology but usually studies a single document state; revision lineage and message-to-attachment references are normally absent.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Document classification or key-value extraction that uses layout but does not preserve evidence locations or cross-version identity.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Abbreviation commonly used for visually rich document understanding, covering joint textual, visual, and layout reasoning.
seed_audit.main_risk: The abbreviation is not uniformly used across papers and can miss relevant work that spells out the task.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Broad document-understanding papers using VRDU as an umbrella while evaluating only classification or field extraction.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Detection, segmentation, classification, and organization of page components such as text blocks, titles, figures, tables, columns, and their spatial relationships.
seed_audit.main_risk: Layout segmentation alone does not establish semantic interpretation, version correspondence, or reference grounding.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Page segmentation, document zoning, OCR preprocessing, and object detection with no semantic or provenance evaluation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Language or vision-language models that encode text together with two-dimensional position, page layout, image features, or structural relations.
seed_audit.main_risk: Model architecture is not itself evidence that exact regions, cells, reading order, or revisions are preserved.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Document classification and token labeling using bounding boxes without evidence localization or cross-version reasoning.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Extraction of structured fields, entities, relations, key-value pairs, or records from documents.
seed_audit.main_risk: Many systems optimize field accuracy while discarding source-location fidelity, unsupported regions, reading order, and revision provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Invoice or receipt field extraction, named-entity recognition, template extraction, and key-value extraction with no exact evidence trace.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Question answering over document images using textual and visual/layout evidence.
seed_audit.main_risk: Most DocVQA work evaluates answer correctness rather than exact provenance or message-to-document reference resolution.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Answer-only benchmarks, single-page QA, OCR-token QA without region evidence, and general VQA on non-document images.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Established benchmark/task label for visual question answering over document images.
seed_audit.main_risk: A paper may be categorized as DocVQA while returning only answer strings and providing no persistent source-region identifier or revision lineage.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Leaderboard-oriented answer generation, synthetic QA, and single-document QA without evidence localization.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Models and benchmarks that reason across multiple pages while retaining page-level context and cross-page relationships.
seed_audit.main_risk: Multi-page processing does not imply stable page-region provenance, completeness, or cross-version alignment.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Page ranking followed by answer generation, document classification, or aggressive page compression with no exact evidence trace.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Understanding long documents containing text, page images, layout, figures, tables, or other modalities under large-context constraints.
seed_audit.main_risk: The term is broad and often focuses on context length or efficiency rather than structural preservation and provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Long-context language modeling, document summarization, or multimodal compression without region/cell grounding.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Non-canonical phrase referring to methods combining OCR output with spatial layout or page structure.
seed_audit.main_risk: Search engines may separate OCR and layout rather than find a recognized task family; OCR quality can dominate results.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: OCR recognition accuracy, text-line detection, character segmentation, and OCR post-correction with no semantic structure.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Determination or reconstruction of the intended sequence among text blocks or page elements, particularly in multi-column or complex layouts.
seed_audit.main_risk: Usually evaluated independently from downstream semantic correctness and provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Simple geometric sorting, OCR line ordering, or layout segmentation without evaluation of decision-relevant content preservation.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Localization of table regions within page images or documents.
seed_audit.main_risk: Only identifies table boundaries; it does not recover rows, columns, spanning cells, units, formulas, or semantics.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Object detection of table bounding boxes and page segmentation benchmarks.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Recovery of a table's structural grid and relationships, including rows, columns, cells, headers, and often spanning cells.
seed_audit.main_risk: Typically concerns rendered tables rather than full workbook semantics or revised-workbook lineage.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Table detection only, HTML reconstruction scored structurally but without semantic reasoning, and clean scientific-table extraction.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Semantic interpretation and reasoning over table structure, headers, values, relationships, and sometimes surrounding context.
seed_audit.main_risk: The term spans both document tables and already-structured relational tables; many papers assume structure is given.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Relational-table representation learning, web-table classification, and database QA with no document extraction problem.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Answering natural-language questions using one or more tabular data sources.
seed_audit.main_risk: Most benchmarks start from clean tables and therefore bypass extraction, visual layout, workbook features, and source provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: WikiTableQuestions-style QA, text-to-SQL, semantic parsing, and clean CSV reasoning.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Interpretation of spreadsheet workbooks beyond flat tables, potentially including cell roles, formulas, regions, sheets, layout, and business semantics.
seed_audit.main_risk: Recent LLM work may reduce workbooks to selected cell ranges or textual encodings and omit hidden structures, formulas, named ranges, formatting semantics, and revision history.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Single-sheet table QA, CSV reasoning, spreadsheet formula synthesis, and cell editing without workbook-wide semantic coverage.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Extraction and interpretation of chart structure, labels, graphical marks, data values, trends, and relationships.
seed_audit.main_risk: Charts are only one attachment subtype and this term will not recover the central version-lineage or workbook-provenance literature.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Chart classification, chart-to-text generation, aesthetic analysis, and data extraction without source grounding.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Question answering over charts using visual marks, labels, legends, axes, and underlying numerical relationships.
seed_audit.main_risk: Useful for structured visual evidence but generally independent of document versioning, message references, and attachment identity.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Standalone chart benchmarks with no document context or region provenance.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Extraction of entities, relations, events, fields, or structured records using multiple modalities such as text, images, and layout.
seed_audit.main_risk: The phrase spans social-media and natural-image tasks as well as documents.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Image-text entity extraction from social media, multimedia event extraction, and generic vision-language extraction unrelated to documents.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Resolution of expressions whose antecedents or referents may occur in different modalities, such as language referring to visible entities.
seed_audit.main_risk: Much of the literature concerns dialogue, video, embodied environments, or natural images rather than document objects.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Video coreference, embodied dialogue, natural-image coreference, and language-only coreference mislabeled as multimodal.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Resolution of referring expressions across modality boundaries, such as language referring to visual objects or regions.
seed_audit.main_risk: Terminology is less standardized than visual grounding or referring-expression comprehension and can retrieve multimedia alignment rather than reference resolution.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Image-text retrieval, representation alignment, audiovisual correspondence, and generic cross-modal matching.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Linking linguistic expressions to visual entities, regions, coordinates, or objects.
seed_audit.main_risk: Dominated by natural-image and GUI datasets; transfer to tables, cells, highlighted rows, and revised documents is not automatic.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Natural-image object grounding, phrase grounding, robotics, navigation, and GUI clicking with no document semantics.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Identifying the visual object or region denoted by a natural-language referring expression.
seed_audit.main_risk: Classical benchmarks assume visible objects in natural scenes rather than document structures or external email messages.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: RefCOCO/ReferIt-style natural-scene grounding with no text/layout/table structure.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Emerging/non-uniform term for mapping language, answers, or extracted facts to spatial regions in a document.
seed_audit.main_risk: Not yet a single standardized task name; searching only the exact phrase may miss papers using evidence localization, phrase grounding, answer grounding, or region attribution.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Generic object detection, page segmentation, and answer extraction that lacks an explicit language-to-region mapping.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Ambiguous term that can mean locating evidence supporting a citation, identifying citation contexts in scholarly articles, or grounding generated claims to source passages.
seed_audit.main_risk: Academic citation-analysis literature uses the same words for a substantially different task.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Citation-context detection, bibliometrics, citation recommendation, scientific citation intent classification, and source-document retrieval without page/region localization.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Understanding document pages available primarily as raster images, often requiring OCR, layout recovery, and visual reasoning.
seed_audit.main_risk: Frequently collapses into OCR or classification rather than evaluating complete structural preservation.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: OCR-only scanned-text recognition, document classification, and archive digitization without semantic grounding.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Comparison of two or more revisions to identify additions, deletions, changes, or structural correspondence.
seed_audit.main_risk: Not a tightly standardized academic task; search results can be dominated by software tools, legal redlining, or lexical diff algorithms without semantic element lineage.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Text diff utilities, document management products, legal redline software, and file-level version control.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Comparison of rendered document pages or screenshots to detect visual changes.
seed_audit.main_risk: Pixel or layout change detection does not establish semantic equivalence, stable element identity, or provenance lineage.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Image registration, screenshot regression testing, pixel diff, webpage visual regression, and change detection without semantic correspondence.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Product-oriented phrase for extracting content from files attached to messages; it is not a well-established academic task name.
seed_audit.main_risk: Likely to retrieve implementation guides and email-processing products rather than peer-reviewed semantic document research.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Email parsing libraries, MIME handling, malware scanning, e-discovery tooling, and commercial attachment extraction.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Product-target description rather than a standard academic task; it suggests joint reasoning over message text and attached documents.
seed_audit.main_risk: The wording may have very sparse academic coverage despite being close to the product problem.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Email attachment classification, malware detection, attachment recommendation, MIME analysis, and email search.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Broad understanding of screenshots, especially user interfaces, webpages, mobile screens, and visually rendered text.
seed_audit.main_risk: Modern literature is strongly dominated by GUI agents and action prediction rather than workplace-document evidence.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: GUI navigation, click prediction, UI code generation, webpage reconstruction, and screen summarization without document grounding.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Alignment of figures or figure regions with captions, textual mentions, or visual content.
seed_audit.main_risk: Useful only for a narrow subset of document evidence and can distract from tables, spreadsheets, revisions, and message references.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Figure-caption matching, scientific figure retrieval, caption generation, and image-text contrastive learning.

seed_audit.academic_meaning: Retrieval of documents, pages, or document passages using textual and visual representations.
seed_audit.main_risk: Retrieval is primarily Topic 07's responsibility and does not establish interpretation, reference grounding, or exact evidence provenance.
seed_audit.false_positive_literature: Document search, multimodal RAG, page retrieval, dense retrieval, cross-modal retrieval, and ranking without source-object grounding.

task_families.name: Cross-version document element alignment and semantic document differencing
task_families.description: Align elements, regions, paragraphs, tables, figures, or other document objects across successive revisions and distinguish unchanged, moved, modified, inserted, deleted, split, and merged content.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is the closest academic family to gap-1. It can supply version-relative correspondence and semantic-change mechanisms, but must be screened for stable lineage rather than mere pairwise diff.
seed_papers: VersionRAG (prior-round admitted seed; bibliographic details not supplied in this prompt)
arXiv:2607.14117 (prior-round admitted seed on cross-version element alignment; title not supplied in this prompt)

task_families.name: Versioned artifact provenance and revision lineage
task_families.description: Represent provenance across versions of an artifact, including stable entity identity, derivation, revision history, change lineage, and mappings between earlier and later states.
task_families.why_it_matters: Database provenance, scientific-workflow provenance, data versioning, and structured-artifact lineage provide representation ideas for attachment revisions, but normally do not model page regions or workplace documents.
seed_papers: Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance (Buneman, Khanna, and Tan, 2001)
Provenance Semirings (Green, Karvounarakis, and Tannen, 2007)

task_families.name: Document-object visual grounding and referring-expression comprehension
task_families.description: Resolve language such as a demonstrative, spatial phrase, row description, or highlighted-object description to a specific document object, region, table component, or coordinate.
task_families.why_it_matters: This family directly targets the mechanism required by gap-2 once it is instantiated on documents rather than natural scenes.

task_families.name: Natural-scene referring-expression grounding
task_families.description: Resolve referring expressions to visual objects or regions in natural images.
task_families.why_it_matters: Provides mature objectives, annotation schemes, region matching, negative examples, and ambiguity handling for references such as 'this screenshot' or 'the highlighted row', but domain transfer to documents must be demonstrated.
seed_papers: ReferItGame: Referring to Objects in Photographs of Natural Scenes (Kazemzadeh et al., 2014)

task_families.name: Multimodal coreference and visually grounded dialogue
task_families.description: Resolve references whose antecedents are visual objects or earlier multimodal conversational context, including conversational ellipsis and demonstratives.
task_families.why_it_matters: Email or Teams language referring into an attachment is structurally closer to cross-modal discourse grounding than to standalone image captioning.
seed_papers: Visual Dialog (Das et al., 2017)

task_families.name: Evidence-grounded document visual question answering
task_families.description: Answer questions over document pages while identifying the page, text span, bounding box, region, table cell, or other evidence supporting the answer.
task_families.why_it_matters: Provides the most direct route to gap-4 if evidence annotations are explicit rather than inferred from OCR tokens after evaluation.
seed_papers: DocVQA: A Dataset for VQA on Document Images
QASPER: A Dataset for Question Answering over Scientific Research Papers

task_families.name: Workbook-level spreadsheet understanding
task_families.description: Interpret spreadsheets as structured workbooks containing multiple sheets, formulas, labels, tables, formatting, merged cells, hidden content, named ranges, and cross-sheet relationships.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is the core search family for gap-3 and must be distinguished from clean-table QA or single-range spreadsheet prompting.
seed_papers: SpreadsheetLLM: Encoding Spreadsheets for Large Language Models
SheetCopilot

task_families.name: Spreadsheet formula dependency, change impact, versioning, and cell lineage
task_families.description: Analyze formula-reference graphs, dependencies, cell derivation, changes between spreadsheet versions, and provenance from outputs back to source cells.
task_families.why_it_matters: Gap-3 cannot be closed by workbook QA alone; formula dependencies and revision lineage require spreadsheet-specific program-analysis and provenance literature.

task_families.name: Table structure recognition and semantic table understanding
task_families.description: Recover table boundaries and logical structure, including rows, columns, headers, spanning or merged cells, and relationships required to interpret values and units.
task_families.why_it_matters: Supports preservation of row/column association and merged relationships and provides structural primitives needed for table-cell grounding.
seed_papers: PubTables-1M: Towards Comprehensive Table Extraction From Unstructured Documents

task_families.name: Document layout analysis, reading-order reconstruction, and scanned-document structure
task_families.description: Recover page zones, element classes, text blocks, reading order, and structure from born-digital or scanned documents.
task_families.why_it_matters: Provides the mechanical substrate for gap-6 and gap-8, especially irregular reading order, scans, embedded objects, and region coordinates.
seed_papers: The Document Spectrum for Page Layout Analysis (O'Gorman, 1993)
LayoutLM: Pre-training of Text and Layout for Document Image Understanding (2020)

task_families.name: Multimodal document information extraction with source localization
task_families.description: Extract fields, entities, relations, or structured facts from documents while preserving the page and region from which each extracted item originated.
task_families.why_it_matters: Bridges extraction and provenance; admission should require explicit localization rather than field accuracy alone.
seed_papers: LayoutLM: Pre-training of Text and Layout for Document Image Understanding (2020)
LayoutLMv2: Multi-modal Pre-training for Visually-Rich Document Understanding (2021)

task_families.name: Hierarchical evidence provenance and fine-grained source attribution
task_families.description: Represent an answer or claim as derived from a hierarchy of source identifiers such as artifact version, page or sheet, element, region or cell, and textual answer span.
task_families.why_it_matters: The exact hierarchy in gap-4 is product-specific. Database provenance, evidence-attribution, QA evidence annotation, and traceability literature can supply compositional models, but the complete hierarchy must not be claimed as already validated.
seed_papers: Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance (Buneman, Khanna, and Tan, 2001)
Provenance Semirings (Green, Karvounarakis, and Tannen, 2007)
QASPER: A Dataset for Question Answering over Scientific Research Papers

task_families.name: Unanswerable document QA, abstention, and failure-aware grounding
task_families.description: Distinguish supported answers from absence of evidence, ambiguous evidence, unanswerable questions, or failures in OCR, parsing, retrieval, localization, or grounding.
task_families.why_it_matters: Gap-5 requires a richer engineering contract than generic unanswerable QA, but selective prediction and unanswerability research provide evaluation patterns for explicit failure rather than silent empty output.
seed_papers: Know What You Don't Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD (SQuAD 2.0, 2018)

task_families.name: Long and multi-page multimodal document reasoning
task_families.description: Reason over many pages or very large document contexts while handling page selection, compression, memory constraints, and cross-page evidence.
task_families.why_it_matters: Targets gap-7 and exposes whether scaling methods preserve exact evidence rather than only answer accuracy.
seed_papers: MP-DocVQA: Multi-page Document Visual Question Answering

task_families.name: Screenshot and GUI grounding
task_families.description: Ground language instructions or referring expressions to regions, text, icons, widgets, or coordinates in screenshots and rendered user interfaces.
task_families.why_it_matters: Provides useful mechanisms for 'this screenshot', highlighted regions, and spatial references, but GUI action grounding must not be treated as evidence of document-table semantics.
seed_papers: SeeClick: Harnessing GUI Grounding for Advanced Visual GUI Agents
ScreenAI: A Vision-Language Model for UI and Infographics Understanding

task_families.name: Chart and structured-graphic question answering with evidence
task_families.description: Interpret charts and structured graphics, reason over their labels, marks, legends, axes, and values, and preferably localize the evidence used.
task_families.why_it_matters: Charts are a relevant but secondary attachment class; this family closes coverage holes without substituting for document, table, or spreadsheet research.
seed_papers: ChartQA

task_families.name: Document extraction robustness and structural-preservation evaluation
task_families.description: Evaluate parsers and document-understanding pipelines under heterogeneous layouts, scans, OCR errors, sparse tables, merged structures, embedded images, and unusual reading order.
task_families.why_it_matters: This is the academic precursor to the engineering test suite required by gap-6 and the joint evaluation required by gap-8.

demoted_terms: visual document differencing when used without semantic alignment
downgrade_rules: Downgrade OCR-only work that measures character, word, or line recognition but does not preserve document structure, source regions, or downstream meaning.
Downgrade document classification work unless it contributes explicit region, element, or provenance mechanisms relevant to the target gaps.
Downgrade generic visually rich document models when evaluation is limited to class labels or extracted fields and does not preserve evidence localization.
Downgrade DocVQA papers that return only an answer string and provide no page, region, bounding-box, cell, token-span, or equivalent supporting-evidence annotation.
Downgrade generic VQA on natural images to TRANSFER unless the task explicitly grounds referring expressions or evidence regions.
Downgrade referring-expression literature on natural scenes to TRANSFER; it cannot establish email-to-attachment accuracy.
Downgrade GUI or screenshot click-grounding work to TRANSFER unless it reasons about document-specific structures such as text blocks, rows, columns, tables, or cells.
Downgrade multimodal coreference work to TRANSFER when its referents are natural-image objects, video entities, embodied environments, or dialogue participants rather than document elements.
Downgrade citation-context detection, citation recommendation, bibliometrics, and scientific citation-intent work; these do not constitute document evidence localization.
Downgrade citation-generation work that cites a whole URL, document, or paper but does not localize the supporting page, region, cell, or span.

Downgrade retrieval and multimodal RAG papers that identify only documents or pages. Retrieval belongs primarily to Topic 07 unless the paper additionally validates exact evidence grounding within the retrieved artifact.
Downgrade version-aware retrieval if version identity only selects the correct snapshot and there is no element correspondence, semantic change representation, or lineage across revisions.
Downgrade ordinary text diff, redline, and edit-distance work unless it establishes structural or semantic correspondence between document elements.
Downgrade pixel-level or screenshot visual differencing unless changed visual regions are linked to persistent semantic document objects.
Downgrade file hashes, duplicate detection, filename heuristics, and attachment identifiers as solutions to version lineage; they can support identity but do not establish semantic correspondence.
Downgrade source-code version-control or AST-diff literature to TRANSFER unless its lineage representation is explicitly portable to document or spreadsheet structures.
Downgrade database provenance to TRANSFER unless the paper directly handles documents or spreadsheets with spatial or cell-level source locations.
Downgrade table-detection-only work for questions concerning table semantics, merged cells, headers, units, or cell-level grounding.
Downgrade clean-table QA and text-to-SQL when the input table is already structured and therefore bypasses extraction, layout, merged cells, workbook context, or provenance.

Downgrade spreadsheet work that serializes a selected range to plain text or CSV and does not demonstrate workbook-level handling of formulas, multiple sheets, hidden structures, cross-sheet references, merged cells, formatting semantics, units, or named ranges.
Downgrade spreadsheet formula generation or repair that does not model provenance, dependency structure, or workbook semantics.
Downgrade single-cell or single-sheet manipulation benchmarks as evidence for comprehensive workbook understanding.
Downgrade document-version studies that compare only metadata, timestamps, filenames, or complete text strings without stable element identity.
Downgrade layout-analysis papers that detect regions but never evaluate reading order or preservation of semantic relationships when those capabilities are required by the claimed finding.
Downgrade parser throughput, latency, or cost papers when they do not measure extraction completeness or meaning preservation.

Downgrade benchmark papers that report only semantic answer accuracy when the project gap requires exact provenance, unsupported-evidence behavior, or preservation of tables, images, and reading order.
Downgrade work that silently treats parser failure, OCR failure, no detected evidence, and genuinely absent evidence as the same empty result.
Downgrade figure-caption alignment and chart-only work to secondary evidence unless the finding specifically concerns figures or charts.
Downgrade email NLP that merely extracts attachment names, MIME metadata, or attachment presence; it does not ground message language into attachment content.
Do not admit product blogs, API documentation, commercial intelligent-document-processing pages, or parser feature lists as academic evidence, although they may later inform ENGINEERING gaps.

Do not infer workplace-email validity from synthetic, scientific-document, natural-image, GUI, or web-document benchmarks; label such evidence TRANSFER unless the evaluation domain actually contains workplace messages and attachments.

Do not treat pairwise alignment as persistent lineage automatically. A method must address identity through multiple revisions, including insertions, deletions, moves, splits, merges, or other correspondence changes, before it supports a stable-lineage claim.
Do not treat a bounding box alone as complete provenance when version, page or sheet, element identity, and answer span are also required.

Do not treat successful extraction of visible spreadsheet cells as comprehensive workbook support when hidden rows, hidden sheets, formulas, named ranges, merged regions, formatting semantics, units, or cross-sheet references are untested.

date_policy.rationale: Discovery should reach at least 1990. The modern multimodal and language-model terminology is recent, but core document layout analysis, page segmentation, reading-order recovery, table recognition, and document-image structure research was already active in the early 1990s. Starting only with the DocVQA/LayoutLM era would silently remove foundational document-analysis work needed to understand structural preservation and failure modes. The version-lineage, multimodal grounding, spreadsheet-LLM, and evidence-attribution subfields can be searched more heavily from the 2000s or 2010s onward, but the global discovery floor should remain 1990 so foundational document-analysis and table-structure work is not excluded.
